healthcareSystem: Public and private healthcare. Libreville has the best facilities including Centre Hospitalier de Libreville and several private clinics. Albert Schweitzer Hospital in Lambaréné is historically significant. Healthcare quality drops dramatically outside urban centers.
qualityNotes: Healthcare in Libreville is adequate for basic and moderate conditions, especially at private clinics. Public hospitals face equipment shortages and staffing issues. Rural areas have extremely limited medical access. Oil wealth has funded some improvements but disparities remain. Serious conditions often require evacuation to South Africa or Europe.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-12:30pm and 3pm-7pm weekdays, Saturday mornings. Duty pharmacies available in Libreville for after-hours needs.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Libreville are reasonably stocked with French medications. Staff speak French. Bring all needed medications for travel outside Libreville. Counterfeit drugs are a concern — use established pharmacies only.
prescriptionRules: Prescription medications require a doctor's ordonnance. In practice, enforcement varies. Bring all medications from home with original packaging and prescriptions.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled narcotics
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription. Keep in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Requires proper documentation for import. Carry prescriptions and a doctor's letter.

bringDocumentation: Bring prescriptions (French translations helpful), a doctor's letter, yellow fever vaccination certificate (required), travel insurance documentation, and copies of all medical records for any ongoing conditions.

travelInsurance.tips: Essential for travel to Gabon. Ensure coverage includes medical evacuation to South Africa or Europe. Private clinic costs can be substantial. Many facilities require cash payment upfront.

recommended: Routine vaccinations (MMR, diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis, varicella, polio, flu)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever vaccination is REQUIRED for all travelers. Malaria is widespread throughout Gabon — take prophylaxis, use mosquito nets, and apply insect repellent. Consult a travel medicine clinic 4-6 weeks before departure.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink. Use only bottled or purified water for drinking, brushing teeth, and making ice. Boil water if bottled water is unavailable.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid raw vegetables, salads, and unpeeled fruits. Be cautious with bushmeat. Stick to bottled beverages. Hotel restaurants in Libreville are generally safe.
medicalTourismNote: Gabon is not a medical tourism destination. The Albert Schweitzer Hospital in Lambaréné is of historical interest but not a tourist medical facility.
sources: French Ministry of Foreign Affairs Travel Advisory
metaDescription: Gabon health guide for travelers: vaccinations, hospitals, malaria prevention, water safety, and insurance.

hospitals.name: Centre Hospitalier de Libreville (CHL)
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital. French-speaking. Emergency department available. Equipment and supply limitations. Overcrowding can be an issue.

hospitals.name: Polyclinique El Rapha
hospitals.notes: Well-regarded private clinic in Libreville. Higher-quality care than public facilities. French-speaking. Cash or card payment upfront.

hospitals.name: Hôpital Albert Schweitzer
hospitals.notes: Historic hospital founded by Albert Schweitzer. Provides care in the Lambaréné area. Limited specialist services.

dentalCare.availability: Limited dental clinics in Libreville. Virtually no dental care outside the capital.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care quality varies. Private clinics in Libreville offer better care. Address dental issues before travel.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies in Libreville, seek a private dental clinic. Outside Libreville, travel to the capital for treatment.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line available.
mentalHealth.internationalLine: Contact your embassy for referrals or use international telehealth services.
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Extremely limited. Most practitioners speak French only.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited in Gabon. Cultural stigma around mental health remains significant. Consider telehealth with your home-country provider.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Gabon.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals in Libreville have basic access but are not fully wheelchair adapted.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads can be in poor condition, especially outside Libreville.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility challenges should plan carefully. National parks and ecotourism sites are generally not wheelchair accessible. Hire local assistance if needed.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mandatory mask requirements. May be requested in healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at major hospitals and private labs in Libreville.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity for respiratory illness is limited outside Libreville. Bring personal health supplies.

insuranceClaimProcess: Most facilities require upfront cash payment. Obtain detailed receipts and medical reports in French. Submit claims to your insurer upon return. Translation of documents may be needed for non-French insurers.

commonCosts.currency: XAF (Central African CFA Franc), prices shown in USD equivalent
commonCosts.note: Private clinic costs are significantly higher than public facilities. Gabon is one of the more expensive countries in Central Africa due to oil wealth.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is essential for serious conditions. International SOS and other providers operate in the region. Oil company medical networks may assist in emergencies.
